title: Hang a door on a pin hinge
instruction: Hang the door on the hinge post: hold its knuckles between the post's knuckles and drop the pin down through all five.
context: Installers and maintenance workers hang doors, gates and access panels on lift-off pin hinges: one hand holds the door with its knuckles lined up, since nothing else supports it until the pin is in, while the other drops the pin.
setup: Between the arms, 26 cm in front of the arm bases: a fixed grey steel hinge post, a leaf 8.7 cm tall with three square knuckles (28 mm outside, 18 mm square hole, 12 mm tall, 18 mm apart, the lowest 3 mm above the table) on a vertical axis. In front of the right arm: a white solid PVC door (12 cm wide, 8 cm tall, 1.2 cm thick, 0.2 kg) standing on its long edge, its hinge edge 16 cm from the post's axis and toward it, held upright near that edge by a grey plastic holder (two 1 x 4 x 3 cm blocks, 14 mm apart, centred 26 cm forward and 19.9 cm right of the post's axis); its hinge edge carries two matching steel knuckles that fit the gaps between the post's. In front of the left arm: a hollow steel hinge pin (10 mm shaft with a rounded nose, 8.5 cm long, under a 22 mm head 6 mm thick, 40 g) standing in a grey plastic square socket (11 mm hole, 3 cm deep, walls 1 cm thick), centred 20 cm forward and 17 cm left of the post's axis.
scoring: 1.0 if the pin, within 10 degrees of upright, passes through all three of the post's knuckles and both of the door's (at each knuckle's height its axis is inside the knuckle's 18 mm hole: within 6 mm of the centre along each side), the door's lowest point is at least 4 mm above the table, and door and pin are still for 1 second. Otherwise, if the pin passes through at least one of the post's knuckles, 0.4 for each of the door's knuckles it passes through (0.8 at most). Pinning only the post's knuckles, or only the door's, scores 0.
reset_notes: Take the pin out and stand it in its socket; stand the door back in its holder.
fidelity: All parts are rigid, built from boxes, cylinders and a sphere (the pin's nose), with the station's default contact material. The knuckles are square rings instead of round barrels, leaving the 10 mm pin 4 mm of play each way in its 18 mm hole, as on a loose real hinge; hung, the door sags about 3 degrees on the pin. Nothing is deformable.
